messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: Not Specified
Medical Record Number: Not Specified
Date of Admission: Not Specified
Date of Discharge: Not Specified

INTRODUCTION:
The patient is an 81-year-old woman who visited the department of internal medicine in our hospital with complaints of loss of appetite, abdominal distension, and an upper abdominal mass. She had a history of left breast cancer 11 years ago. The patient was diagnosed with peritoneal metastasis of recurrent breast cancer and was put on endocrine therapy using letrozole.

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient's symptoms improved with endocrine therapy, and she showed recovery from pleural metastasis and pleural effusion. Tumor marker values fluctuated during the course of treatment, with no abnormal CEA values obtained, and CA15-3 and BCA225 values gradually declining from the time of recurrence and returning to normal levels 2 years later. NCC-ST-439 value gradually increased up to 49 U/ml 6 months later, with a gradual decline thereafter along with the other tumor markers. The patient was currently receiving treatment in the outpatient department and is still alive on the same medication.

DISCHARGE OUTCOME:
The patient is being discharged in stable condition with continued endocrine therapy.

FOLLOW-UP:
No relapse of malignancy has been detected after a period of 6 years.

ATTENDING PHYSICIAN:
Not Specified
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Letrozole.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
Continue endocrine therapy as prescribed. Follow up with your healthcare provider as recommended.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
This is recurrent breast cancer with peritoneal metastasis, treated with letrozole. The pleural metastasis and effusion are also mentioned. The principal diagnosis is the secondary malignancy treated during the admission, which is peritoneal metastasis. In ICD-10-AM, secondary malignant neoplasm of the retroperitoneum and peritoneum is C78.6, so the category is C78.

The alternative would be C50, for the primary breast cancer, but it was treated 11 years ago and the current treatment is directed at the metastatic disease. This follows the pattern in Example 6, where metastases were coded to the secondary site (C79) rather than the primary.

C78
